shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading 1×A for 1×B would make my inventory less balanced (A:0, B:2, C:1). Since I value variety and currently have an even mix, this reduces my utility.
Starting from an even 1A,1B,1C bundle, swapping 1B for 1A would make my inventory less balanced (2A,0B,1C). Since I value variety and currently value all goods equally, this trade reduces my utility.

Trading 1 B for 2 A changes my inventory from (1,1,1) to (3,0,1). Since all goods are valued equally but variety matters, this is a mixed change; however, receiving 2 units for 1 unit increases my total holdings and is acceptable at this starting balance.
With A=1, B=1, C=1, my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1×C for 1×B would make it less varied (A=1, B=2, C=0), which lowers my utility.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C, so swapping 1 B for 1 C would reduce variety and leave me with 0 B and 2 C, which lowers my utility.

Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory to 1 A, 0 B, 3 C. I value all goods equally but prefer variety, so losing B entirely and becoming more concentrated in C reduces variety and lowers my utility.
Starting from an even bundle of A, B, and C, trading 1 A for 1 B would reduce variety and leave me with more B and no A, which lowers my utility.
Starting from a balanced bundle of 1A, 1B, and 1C, trading 1B for 1A would make my inventory less varied (2A, 0B, 1C), which lowers utility given my preference for variety.

Starting from a balanced bundle (1,1,1), trading 1×B for 2×A gives me (3,0,1). Since all goods are equally valuable and I prefer variety, this is worse: I lose all of B and become less balanced. The extra A does not offset that loss in variety.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C. Trading 1×C for 1×B would leave me with less variety and a more imbalanced bundle, so it does not improve my utility.
Starting from an even bundle of 1A, 1B, 1C, trading 1B for 1C would make my inventory less balanced (1A, 0B, 2C). Since I value variety and currently value all goods equally, this reduces my utility.

Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory from (1,1,1) to (1,0,3). The total quantity increases, and despite reduced variety, the gain of two goods for one improves my bundle overall.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves my variety by turning inventory from A:2, B:0, C:2 into A:1, B:1, C:2. Since I currently have no B and prefer goods I have less of, receiving B increases my utility.

This trade increases variety by converting surplus A into my missing good B. My inventory would go from (A2,B0,C2) to (A0,B1,C2), which better matches my preference for balanced holdings, and B is also currently strategically valuable.

Trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety in my inventory: I currently have no B and more C, so gaining B is more valuable than keeping an extra C. The market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable.
I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B increases variety and balances my inventory. Giving 2 C reduces a surplus relative to B, and the market bulletin suggests B is strategically valuable.

Trading 1 A for 1 B improves my variety: I currently have no B, so gaining B is especially valuable while reducing A from 2 to 1 still leaves a more balanced bundle. The market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable.

This trade increases variety by converting surplus A into B, which I currently lack entirely. It changes my inventory from (A2,B0,C3) to (A0,B1,C3), improving balance, and B is also flagged as strategically valuable in the market.
I currently have no B and a surplus of C, so exchanging 1 C for 1 B increases variety and improves my bundle. The market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable.
I currently have no B and excess C, so gaining 1 B in exchange for 2 C increases variety and balances my inventory. The market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable.
I currently have no B and equal amounts of A and C, so receiving 1 B and giving 1 A improves variety in my inventory. The market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable.
I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B strongly improves variety. Giving 2 A leaves me with a more balanced bundle (A:0, B:1, C:2), and the market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable.
Trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety in my inventory: I currently have no B, so gaining B and reducing surplus C increases my utility. The market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable.

I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B strongly improves variety, while giving 2 C reduces a good I have in relative surplus. The resulting bundle is more balanced, and B also appears strategically valuable in the market.

Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from A1 B1 C2 to A0 B2 C2. Since A and B were tied as my scarcest goods, this does not improve variety on its own, but market information indicates B is currently strategically more valuable, so receiving B in exchange for A increases my utility.

Giving up 1 B for 1 A would change my inventory from A1,B1,C2 to A2,B0,C2, reducing variety by eliminating B entirely. Since I prefer a balanced mix and B is also currently strategically valuable in the market, this trade lowers my utility.

Giving up 1 B is not worth receiving 2 A here. I currently need more variety, but B is also strategically important in the market and not more plentiful than A after this trade; the exchange would reduce my flexibility rather than improve my bundle.

Trading 1 C for 1 B changes my inventory from (A1,B1,C2) to (A1,B2,C1), which is more balanced and reduces my surplus of C. The market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable, so this improves my bundle.

Giving up 1 B for 1 C would worsen my variety: my inventory would go from A1/B1/C2 to A1/B0/C3, eliminating B entirely and increasing an already more abundant good. The market bulletin also suggests B is strategically valuable.

Trading 2 C for 1 B changes my inventory from (A1,B1,C2) to (A1,B2,C0). While variety decreases slightly, C is my most abundant good and B is strategically more valuable in the current market, so this improves my expected utility.
Giving up my only B would reduce variety, and B is currently strategically valuable in the market. Although I would gain more C, I already have more C than A or B, so this trade lowers my utility.
